$comment: ⛔ THE CROSS-LANGUAGE PARITY FIXTURE FOR THE `derivation` EVIDENCE KIND (kb/Work PB386, 2026-09-03).
kb/Work PB315 is the note recording what happens when `Schema.state_for` and its C# twin `DerivedState` read
one rule differently: the disagreement was UNOBSERVABLE until a row first exercised the divergent branch, and
it then sat there for a day looking like a correct batch. The owner's first stated cost for opening this door
was that both engines learn the evidence kind in the SAME change set — this file is what makes that claim
falsifiable, rather than a sentence in a commit message.
It is a WORLD plus a list of CASES. Each engine builds the world (a fabricated docs/CONFORMANCE.md §8
register, a fabricated §7 item set, a fabricated Annex A.2 resolution, fabricated catalogs of two editions,
each rule-id with its text, and fabricated cobol-refuter record files, kb/Work PB5374), evaluates
every case, and asserts BOTH the derived `state` and the exact set of refusal CODES. Comparing codes rather
than a boolean is the point: two evaluators that reject one row for two different reasons look identical
under 'it was refused', which is the shape PB315 hid behind for months.
⚙ THE WORLD IS FABRICATED ON PURPOSE. Every live determination is correct, so the arms
cannot be falsified against the real document — a fixture built from it would pass for the wrong reason
Python: `python scripts/spec/audit_derivations.py --parity`.  C#: DerivationParityDriftTests, which runs
both and requires the three answers to agree.
